author: Amy Smith
title: A mill that can stay in service

stops.label: Start with the work
stops.detail: Grinding grain by hand takes time and effort. The first picture shows who already does the job.

stops.label: Follow the grain
stops.detail: In a hammermill, fast-moving hammers break grain into small particles. A conventional mill uses a screen to control what leaves.

stops.label: Change the repair
stops.detail: Smith’s screenless design separates particles using air. Removing the screen also removes a part that operators would otherwise have to replace.

author: Shawn Frayne
title: From a pellet to a usable fuel

stops.label: Find a local input
stops.detail: The team tried sawdust available in the village. Availability settled only one part of the design problem.

stops.label: Hold the pellet together
stops.detail: A binder helped the sawdust hold its shape. A pellet that survives handling still has to perform in a stove.

stops.label: Test the burn
stops.detail: The team used the result of burning a sample to guide the next trial. Could a material pass a shape test and still fail the cooking test?

stops.label: Lift the craft
stops.detail: The main rotor must move enough air to lift the craft and its payload.

stops.label: Keep it steady
stops.detail: Look at the arrangement of the rotors. One design problem is controlling the body’s tendency to turn.

stops.label: Test a payload
stops.detail: Drouillard describes adding weights in prototype tests. Holding the craft steady without a load does not show that it can carry one.

stops.label: Start with the solid
stops.detail: Imagine the part inside a transparent box. Each face records the view straight through it.

stops.label: Open the box
stops.detail: Swing the faces outward while keeping the features aligned. The views move apart on the paper.

stops.label: Read the flat drawing
stops.detail: Use matching edges to connect front, top, and side views. A single outline can hide the depth of a feature.

stops.label: Fit the electronics
stops.detail: A smaller circuit assembly can fit a redesigned case. The electrical and mechanical teams need the same space limits.

stops.label: Make the parts
stops.detail: The mechanical design must work with an actual manufacturing method.

stops.label: Put it in someone’s hands
stops.detail: Observe a person using the buttons and display. A working circuit can still be difficult to operate.

author: Araceli Ortiz
title: Move the work past the worker

stops.label: Enter the line
stops.detail: A part reaches a station where a particular operation is ready for it.

stops.label: Repeat one operation
stops.detail: Each station completes its own portion of the work as successive products pass.

stops.label: Look downstream
stops.detail: If one station takes longer than the others, unfinished work can accumulate before it. What would you time?

author: Dudley Green
title: A stencil inside a manufacturing system

stops.label: Identify the input
stops.detail: Circuit boards and material for making connections enter the work station.

stops.label: Locate the process
stops.detail: Green’s stencil controls where material is deposited. Its openings translate the board layout into a repeatable operation.

stops.label: Close the loop
stops.detail: Inspect the output against the intended pattern. Evidence of a misplaced deposit can change the setup for the next board.

author: Christine Epplett
title: Change the shape of shoe material

stops.label: Stack the material
stops.detail: Webbing brings layers together so that the next operation can act on several layers.

stops.label: Cut a part
stops.detail: Separating removes material. The cut outline affects how shoe pieces will fit together.

stops.label: Form a part
stops.detail: A forming operation changes shape by applying force. Compare it with cutting a new outline.

author: Saul Griffith
title: Shape a lens before it hardens

stops.label: Start with a liquid
stops.detail: Liquid acrylic can take the shape of the cavity between two flexible membranes.

stops.label: Set the curvature
stops.detail: The syringes control the membrane shape. A changed curvature makes a different optical surface.

stops.label: Fix the shape
stops.detail: Ultraviolet light hardens the acrylic. The lens keeps the shape set before curing.

author: Peter Park
title: Density and the trip to the store

stops.label: Count residents
stops.detail: Population gives a head count. The number alone does not say how close those people live to one another.

stops.label: Include land area
stops.detail: Compare people per square mile. The denominator matters when comparing two places of different sizes.

stops.label: Trace a real route
stops.detail: Even at the same density, zoning and street connections can change whether residents can walk to a shop. Try the street plan below.

author: Kirk Elwell
title: Trace the load on the Zakim Bridge

stops.label: Start at the deck
stops.detail: A moving vehicle adds load to a deck that already supports its own weight.

stops.label: Follow the cable
stops.detail: The deck pulls on a stay. The cable carries tension along its length.

stops.label: Follow it to ground
stops.detail: Stay forces reach the tower. The tower and foundations carry the load into the ground.

stops.label: Find the base
stops.detail: The tall tower is supported at its foundation. Wind also acts sideways over its height.

stops.label: Follow the changing shape
stops.detail: The tower gets narrower and changes shape with height. Different parts encounter the wind differently.

stops.label: Break the rhythm
stops.detail: Baker compares repeated wind forces with pushing a swing. Varying the profile makes a single organized pushing rhythm harder to sustain.

author: Prity Rungta
title: Stand a floor joist on edge

stops.label: Find the sheathing
stops.detail: Floor sheathing spreads a load to the joists below it.

stops.label: Stand it on edge
stops.detail: A rectangular joist has more depth in this orientation. It resists bending better under a vertical load.

stops.label: Compare it flat
stops.detail: Turn the same piece flat. The material and length stay the same while its resistance to bending changes.

stops.label: Start above ground
stops.detail: Wind pushes a tall tower sideways. Ice can add weight to the supported line.

stops.label: Cross the ground line
stops.detail: The load continues through the base into the buried foundation.

stops.label: Ask what lies below
stops.detail: Soil and rock conditions help determine the needed foundation dimensions. The surface view cannot supply that information.

author: Chris Benedict
title: Compare an equal thickness of wall material

stops.label: Read the columns
stops.detail: Compare the materials on the same basis. This table gives resistance to heat flow per inch.

stops.label: Compare resistance
stops.detail: A higher R-value at equal thickness means more resistance to heat flow.

stops.label: Build a whole wall
stops.detail: The wall includes multiple materials. Look for a continuous path of insulation as well as places where heat can bypass it.

stops.label: Admit the light
stops.detail: Sunlight enters through the glazing. A well-placed overhang can admit lower winter sunlight.

stops.label: Store the energy
stops.detail: A floor or wall with thermal mass absorbs energy and warms up during the day.

stops.label: Release it later
stops.detail: After the room cools, energy can flow from the warmer mass to the room. No fan is required for the storage itself.

stops.label: Balance the forces
stops.detail: Read the starting arrangement in the variable ballast tank. A hovering vehicle has balanced weight and buoyant force.

stops.label: Take water aboard
stops.detail: Adding water increases the vehicle’s mass at nearly fixed external volume. Its weight can exceed buoyant force.

stops.label: Pump water out
stops.detail: Removing water reduces the weight. Watch the direction of the resulting motion in the sequence.

stops.label: Identify the pair
stops.detail: The two objects push on one another during the same interaction.

stops.label: Compare the arrows
stops.detail: The forces on the two different objects point in opposite directions. They do not cancel on either object alone.

stops.label: Transfer it to flight
stops.detail: A spacecraft ejects propellant one way and changes its own momentum the other way. The rocket does not need outside air to push on.

stops.label: Admit and compress air
stops.detail: The piston draws in air and then compresses it. Compressing the air raises its temperature.

stops.label: Deliver the power stroke
stops.detail: Injected fuel ignites in the hot air. Expanding gas drives the piston and turns the crankshaft.

stops.label: Clear the cylinder
stops.detail: The exhaust stroke removes spent gas so the next cycle can begin.

stops.label: Keep the gas inside
stops.detail: This machine reuses a sealed working gas. Energy crosses the boundary while the working gas stays inside.

stops.label: Move gas between ends
stops.detail: The displacer moves gas toward the hot or cool region. Temperature changes affect the pressure.

stops.label: Drive the piston
stops.detail: A changing gas pressure moves the power piston. Repeating the cycle turns the crank.

author: Ron DiPippo
title: From steam flow to electric power

stops.label: Direct the steam
stops.detail: A nozzle directs high-pressure steam toward the turbine blades.

stops.label: Turn the shaft
stops.detail: The steam changes direction at the blades, exerting a force that turns the turbine.

stops.label: Run the generator
stops.detail: The rotating shaft couples the turbine to a generator. The energy pathway continues into an electrical circuit.

stops.label: Begin with a neutron
stops.detail: A uranium nucleus can absorb a neutron and undergo fission.

stops.label: Follow the split
stops.detail: The fission products carry energy away. Additional neutrons may be released.

stops.label: Control the chain
stops.detail: Some neutrons can trigger further events. A power reactor must control that rate to deliver heat steadily.

stops.label: Find the higher surface
stops.detail: The elevated water surface provides a height reference for the supply.

stops.label: Measure the vertical drop
stops.detail: Use the vertical height difference rather than the length of pipe to determine static pressure change.

stops.label: Compare with flow
stops.detail: Once water flows, friction in the pipe also matters. Available pressure and actual flow are different measurements.

author: David Clark
title: Deliver a long message in pieces

stops.label: Divide the message
stops.detail: A packet has a limited size. A larger message must be carried in parts.

stops.label: Keep track of the parts
stops.detail: Each piece needs information that lets the receiving system place it correctly.

stops.label: Reassemble in order
stops.detail: Packets may arrive out of order. Sequence information makes the original order recoverable.

author: Sol Lerner
title: Turn a voice into an electrical signal

stops.label: Reach the microphone
stops.detail: Sound-pressure changes arrive at the diaphragm and make it move.

stops.label: Change the circuit
stops.detail: In the carbon microphone pictured here, diaphragm motion changes the carbon granules’ contact and electrical resistance.

stops.label: Recreate motion
stops.detail: An electrical signal can drive the receiver. Recognizing what was said requires further processing.

stops.label: Enter the core
stops.detail: Light carrying a signal travels in the fiber’s core.

stops.label: Meet the boundary
stops.detail: The core and cladding have different optical properties. Rays at suitable angles reflect internally.

stops.label: Continue down the guide
stops.detail: Successive reflections keep guided light in the fiber until a receiver detects the signal.

author: Alex Hills
title: Relay a call through a satellite

stops.label: Encode the caller
stops.detail: The caller’s equipment converts the message into a signal that the network can transmit.

stops.label: Relay over distance
stops.detail: Ground stations and a satellite relay the signal past gaps in the terrestrial network.

stops.label: Deliver the message
stops.detail: The receiving network brings the signal to the listener. Trace the return trip for a conversation.

stops.label: Read the axes
stops.detail: The graph compares current with voltage for a resistor. Keep resistance fixed.

stops.label: Double the push
stops.detail: At fixed resistance, doubling the voltage doubles the current.

stops.label: Read the slope
stops.detail: A steeper current-versus-voltage line means more current for the same voltage, hence less resistance.

stops.label: Measure power
stops.detail: Power tells how fast energy is being transferred. Start by specifying the useful electrical output.

stops.label: Track energy over time
stops.detail: Energy delivered over an interval depends on the power and duration. Keep units consistent.

stops.label: Compare with the input
stops.detail: Efficiency compares useful output energy with input energy. Some input leaves as heat even in a functioning plant.

stops.label: Trace the first loop
stops.detail: Follow one complete route from the source through one lamp and back.

stops.label: Trace the other branch
stops.detail: Both branches connect across the same two supply points. Each therefore has the same voltage across it.

stops.label: Open one branch
stops.detail: Breaking only one branch leaves a complete path through the other. Test that prediction in the circuit model.

author: Christine Bordonaro
title: Follow energy through a solar cell

stops.label: Light arrives
stops.detail: Incoming light supplies energy to the cell.

stops.label: Separate charges
stops.detail: The layered semiconductor structure helps separate charge and establish a voltage between the contacts.

stops.label: Connect a load
stops.detail: A closed external circuit gives current a route. The cell can then deliver electrical energy to a load.

stops.label: Catch moving air
stops.detail: Wind exerts forces on the blades and turns the rotor.

stops.label: Drive a generator
stops.detail: Rotation passes through the turbine’s drive system and the generator produces electrical power.

stops.label: Connect to shore
stops.detail: The offshore system also needs foundations, cables and a connection to the grid. The rotor alone cannot deliver power to users.
